blocks.x: AI Proof-of-Concept & Value Validation is delivered by an Achala practice team that stays through industrialization. Achala ships applied AI with its evidence attached: evaluation harnesses, drift monitoring and measured deltas against your baseline. If a model does not beat the baseline, we say so — that honesty is why clients keep the programs running. Who this is for: product and business leaders with a P&L line to move, and CDOs consolidating AI governance.

The sprint is engineered backwards from the exit report. Baseline collection starts on day one, the eval set is built before the model is touched, and the final deck is one page of numbers your CFO can audit against the ledger.
Below is the anatomy of the sprint: the failure modes that turn PoCs into demo-ware, the reference architecture for a four-week evidence machine, and the gates the verdict must clear.

blocks.title: AI PoC & value validation — gate console

widgets.title: The four gates — click each for its evidence contract

stages.name: Gate 1 — Feasibility
stages.detail: Candidates run against the frozen case set with identical prompts, identical budgets. Pass bar: beat measured baseline on the primary metric with statistical confidence. No live data, no exceptions.

stages.name: Gate 2 — Economics
stages.detail: Cost model with realistic volumes — model spend, human review load, integration amortization. Pass bar: value hypothesis holds with 50% margin, not a rounding error.

stages.name: Gate 3 — Robustness
stages.detail: Adversarial cases, out-of-distribution inputs, drift simulation. Pass bar: quality degrades gracefully and monitoring catches the degradation before the business does.

stages.name: Gate 4 — Operability
stages.detail: Monitoring wired, fallback path defined, retraining trigger documented, owner named. Pass bar: the run team signs the support contract — not the innovation team.

widgets.note: Four gates, one funding decision. The kill rates are honest: most PoCs should die at Gate 2 or 3 — that is the point of the structure.

widgets.title: Candidate portfolio — value vs readiness
widgets.note: Hover for names and gate status. The upper band is this year's funded slate; the kills are published internally — a visible graveyard is what keeps hypotheses honest.

widgets.title: Total cost of ownership what-if — volume, review load, model class
widgets.note: Review load is the silent TCO killer: each 10% of human review adds roughly a dollar per case and erases the delta on mid-value processes. The curve is the argument for investing in quality before scaling volume.

A PoC verdict is an instrument reading
blocks.sub: The measurement discipline that makes a four-week verdict defensible in a steering committee

blocks.x: Most PoCs measure the wrong thing: demo delight instead of decision-grade deltas. The sprint is instrumented from day one, a provability canvas fixes the metric, the measurement method and the baseline before any model runs; baseline collection measures the human work the model would replace (minutes per case, error rates, rework shares); and the real data path runs production-shaped data under production-shaped governance, so the verdict survives contact with the estate. An integration probe touches at least one real system, because the honest friction, auth, schemas, latency, is where PoC timelines actually die.

The fund/kill gate is the product. At week four the steering committee reads three numbers: delta against baseline on the golden set, cost per unit of work at sprint scale, and the integration gaps with named owners. Fund means a funded delivery slice with a metric; kill means a documented kill reason in the ledger, and both are wins, because the cheapest failed project is the one that costs four weeks.

items: Provability canvas first
Metric, method and baseline signed before a model runs.
Real data path
Production-shaped data under governance; synthetic only where PHI/PII forbids.
Integration probe
One real system, early, friction is evidence, not noise.
Fund/kill with named owner
Three numbers at the gate; kill reasons logged like fund decisions.
Why four weeks — is that realistic for a real verdict?

Four weeks is enough because the sprint is bounded deliberately: one provable slice, a signed baseline, a real data path and a named verdict owner. Ideas that cannot fit that box fail the provability screen before they consume a sprint.
What if the data is not ready in week one?

The data path is a week-1 gate, not a hope: if the data cannot be wired and profiled by the end of week one, the gate kills the sprint and returns the finding, data readiness is a verdict, not a slide.
How do you measure value without a production deployment?

The baseline is signed before week one ends, so the eval set measures delta against a number your finance team has already countersigned, holdout-adjusted, with the measurement method in the verdict pack.
Do we get to keep the code and eval artifacts?
Yes. Baseline, golden eval set, cost model, integration gap list and the verdict pack are yours at verdict time, whatever the verdict is, a kill still leaves you the instrumented evidence.
What makes this different from our innovation team running a pilot?

The gates. A pilot runs on enthusiasm; the sprint runs on kill criteria with named owners, and the fund gate requires a price, a data path and an integration probe, the same evidence a steering committee will ask for at scale.
